territorial_scope.description: Applies as a state statute of Hawaii amending Chapter 481B, Hawaii Revised Statutes; the text does not expressly address operators located outside the state.

evidence.quote: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF HAWAII

summary.short: Adds a section to Hawaii Revised Statutes chapter 481B regulating publicly accessible conversational AI services. Operators must issue AI-disclosure notices, give minors recurring AI disclaimers, adopt suicide and self-harm response protocols, file annual reports, and face enforcement through unfair-practice law and attorney general actions. Section 2 takes effect July 1, 2027.
summary.long: Adds a section to Hawaii Revised Statutes chapter 481B governing publicly accessible conversational AI services. Operators (persons who develop or offer such services to the public) must notify users when a reasonable person would believe they are talking to a human, and must give known minors a disclaimer that they are interacting with AI, repeated at session start and at least every three hours. Operators must adopt protocols for suicidal ideation or self-harm prompts, including referrals to crisis services, and must not represent the service as designed for professional mental health care. For known minors, operators must avoid engagement-driving unpredictable rewards, prevent sexually explicit, romantic or sexual content and manipulative engagement techniques, and offer privacy tools to minors and their parents or guardians. Operators must file annual reports with the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs from January 1, 2028. Violations are unfair or deceptive practices; the attorney general and office of consumer protection may seek injunctive relief and damages, and private actions are barred. Section 6 sets the effective date as July 1, 3000, with section 2 effective July 1, 2027.

thresholds.measurement: age of the account holder or user; no measurement window or method stated
thresholds.consequence: Defines 'minor' for the minor-specific duties in subsections (b) and (d).
thresholds.conditions: Applies where the operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty that the account holder or user is a minor (subsections (b) and (d)).

evidence.quote: "Minor" means any person under eighteen years of age.
"Account holder" or "user" means a person who has or generates an account or profile to use a conversational artificial intelligence service.
"Artificial intelligence" means an engineered or machine‑based system that varies in its level of autonomy

"Conversational artificial intelligence service" or "service" means an artificial intelligence software application, web interface, or computer program that is accessible to the general public that primarily simulates human conversation and interaction through textual, visual, or aural communications.

"Crisis intervention" means communication intended to provide immediate support or assistance in response to a user seeking help for, referencing, or expressing self-harm, suicidal ideation, or suicide.
"Emotional attachment" means a sustained bond that develops through repeated interaction.
"Emotional dependency" means a pattern of interaction in which a minor develops an excessive emotional reliance on a conversational artificial intelligence service.
"Minor" means any person under eighteen years of age.
"Operator" means a person who develops or makes available a conversational artificial intelligence service to the public.

obligations.summary: Operator must issue a clear and conspicuous notification that the conversational AI service is artificial intelligence and not human, where a reasonable person would be led to believe they are interacting with a human.
obligations.applies_from: July 1, 2027 (Sec. 6: section 2 takes effect on July 1, 2027)
obligations.conditional_on: A reasonable person interacting with a conversational AI service would be led to believe the person is interacting with a human

evidence.quote: an operator shall issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the service is artificial intelligence and not human.

obligations.summary: Where the operator knows or reasonably should know a user is a minor, it must disclose to the minor that they are interacting with AI, either as a persistent visible disclaimer or both at the start of each session and at least every three hours, with a reminder to take a break.
obligations.applies_from: July 1, 2027 (Sec. 6: section 2 takes effect on July 1, 2027)
obligations.conditional_on: Operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty that an account holder or user is a minor

evidence.quote: the operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to the minor account holder or user that the minor is interacting with artificial intelligence

obligations.summary: Operator must adopt a protocol for responding to user prompts about suicidal ideation or self-harm, referring users to crisis services; use evidence-based methods for measuring suicidal ideation; and institute reasonable measures to prevent the service from implying it is human to a person seeking crisis intervention for self-harm or suicide.
obligations.applies_from: July 1, 2027 (Sec. 6: section 2 takes effect on July 1, 2027)

evidence.quote: Adopt a protocol for the conversational artificial intelligence service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm

obligations.summary: Operator may not cause or program the conversational AI service to state that it is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care.

obligations.summary: Operator may not provide points or similar rewards to a minor at unpredictable intervals with the intent to increase engagement.
